restrictions: Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge (rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06, pad10*1), prefix rounds 0 through 5, all 256 output bits; every message is exactly 128 bytes (one block; lane 16 = 0x8000000000000006).

Generic birthday search over N = 255*2^120 messages in 255*2^88 groups of 2^32. Group g has a fresh structured 128-byte prefix P_g (5kyguy's family of 6e715d9a): 768 uniform bits in the free lanes 0-4, 6, 7, 9-11, 13, 14; with C4 = L4 ^ L9 ^ L14 and C1 = L1 ^ L6 ^ L11 ^ 0x8000000000000006, L5 = L15 = C4 ^ rotl(C1, 1), L8 = 0, L12 = ~rotl(C4, 1) ^ L2 ^ L7 (the prefix map is injective). Message m(g, z) is P_g with LE32(z) XORed into bytes 32..35 and 112..115 (low halves of lanes 4 and 14, one theta column). This makes round 1 linear in z (linear structures of Guo, Liu and Song, ASIACRYPT 2016; on this track Th0rgal's 4867f093; this family is 5kyguy's). Groups are processed in batches of 256 (one group per bit position of every 256-bit word, bitsliced), z = gray(t) for t = 0..2^32-1, slots offered in the fixed order decode_slot(q) = 16*(q mod 16) + floor(q/16), q = 0..255. The messages with processing indices q = 2k and q = 2k+1 of batch beta at step t share the pair id n = beta*2^39 + t*2^7 + k.

Each z-step of a batch (256 messages) is an exact counted, fully unrolled word-RAM program (branches only in the ctz tree, the table step with its candidate path, and the loop test; 32 fused straight-line leaves) of at most 31,176 executed primitives on its worst path (leaves 31,153..31,176): an AND-free incremental round 2 (z-bit j flips a fixed 22-word set of A2 by all-ones; only the 975 read words are maintained, 3-10 flips per leaf; 499 round-3 input words get fixed XOR patches merged into the round-3 loads; at most 1,764 ops), lane-complement rounds 3-5 with theta at the store and start planes (10, 61, 34), the round 4-5 dependency cones (1,363 and 175 words), the last round on 35 bit planes (140-bit key), a rotating-frame zero-row transpose in a 16-row layout (3,418 ALU ops), a tagged-id table step of 5 ops (even q) or 6 ops (odd q) per message, and loop control. Charge: 31,176/256 + setup (< 2^-20) per message; batch setup is a counted 76,162-op program.

The counted program (generator, compiler, counted simulator, setup generator) and a self-test that regenerates all 33 bodies, asserts the worst-step count 31,176 and checks every body on the simulator against verifier/keccak.py are shipped as proof Appendix A (seven files with SHA-256 markers and an extraction command; package rules admit no other source files and the experiment-source budget is 64 KiB).

Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers as our stated assumption (the program uses all 64: at most 62 per compiled leaf, register-allocated by interval colouring after SSA and store-to-load forwarding, plus the step counter and the table word c). One six-round permutation costs 1 unit; every executed load, store (direct or register-addressed), logic operation, shift or rotation, add, comparison, conditional branch, immediate move and random word costs 1/1626; constant addresses and immediates are instruction fields. The 64-register reading does not cover a register bank of thousands of words; no bound is claimed under such a reading (it would give 123.809 here; not claimed) or a memory-to-memory reading. Charging also one address addition per direct access and one move per ALU immediate gives 40,026 per z-step and 124.622; also each shift or rotation amount 40,812 and 124.650.

Table: S has 2^140 words at address 0 and is never initialised; the key K < 2^140 is the address; the slot holds TAG*2^128 + n, n the pair id of the last message with key K (TAG uniform 128-bit, drawn once per run). Per-message hot path: load, XOR, compare < 2^128, branch, store, and c += 1 after odd q only. A slot whose high half equals TAG is a candidate: the site's own out-of-line copy rebuilds the current message and both members of the stored pair from their ids and stored 4-word prefixes and evaluates them (3 units); it halts only on equal 256-bit digests of distinct messages, else counts the candidate and continues (at most 136 extra ops: 106 path incl. the jump back, measured 97..106, plus 30 state-marshalling ops to form padded state and read digests, all charged; halting charged 136), aborting at the hard cap VCAP = floor(N^2/2^141) + floor(N^2/2^148) + 2^91 + 2^61. Garbage candidates (never-written words) have expectation <= N*2^-128 for any initial memory.

Time bound in every run (no restarts): T <= N*(31,176/256 + 2^-20)/1626 + VCAP*(3 + 136/1626) + (3 + 136/1626) + 1 + 2^50 (allowance for generating the program once) < 2^124.262651, proved by an exact integer inequality: with K = 2^28*1626 and A = T*K (an integer), A^1000000 < 2^124262651 * K^1000000 (proof Section 8; re-derived independently by GordoAR from the shipped Appendix A program: ledger, VCAP pricing and the amortised-setup bound re-checked in exact rationals). Claimed time_log2 = 124.26266, the value OUR recompute supports (2^124.26265 is not reached). Success probability 0.39 (model 0.39106 = 1 - exp(-N(N-1)/2^257) - 4e-5) relies on H1 for F1, F2 and the genuine-candidate abort (<= 2^-100); garbage candidates add <= 2^-61 by Markov, F3 < 2^-545, both unconditional. Memory < 2^145.01 bytes. Output correctness and all resource bounds are unconditional.

The start-plane search, 16-row layout, pair ids, compiler and experiment protocol are ours. None has reviewed this package. Revises our 5e73af65 and 64ee9000.

No cryptanalytic weakness of SHA3 is claimed: this is a constant-factor improvement of a full-digest birthday search under the operation-level cost model. Memory is about 2^145 bytes (reported only, not a Pareto improvement).

heuristics.statement: (a) For the failure events F1, F2 and the genuine-candidate part of F4 (proof Section 7), the N = 255*2^120 digests of the grouped message set {m(g, z)} (independent prefixes P_g, each uniform over the 2^768 structured 128-byte prefixes of Section 2, all z in {0,1}^32, processed in any fixed order chosen independently of the digests, in particular the order of Section 2: batch by batch, t = 0..2^32-1 with z = gray(t), slots p = decode_slot(q) = 16*(q mod 16) + floor(q/16) for q = 0..255) behave like N independent uniform 256-bit values, i.e. Pr[F1] <= exp(-N(N-1)/2^257), Pr[F2] <= N^3/6 * 2^-396 and, since the 140-bit key is a fixed function of 140 digest bits, the number Y1 of message pairs with equal keys has E[Y1] <= N^2/2^141 and Var[Y1] <= E[Y1]. (b) Run-selection premise of the evidence: the organizer-executed configuration (four layouts, 18-bit masks, N_t = 2^9, 256 trials per experiment, per-trial seed derivation by the runner) is unchanged from our public packages 949c283b and 5e73af65; the message family is fixed externally (5kyguy, 6e715d9a; their organizer trials of it were not used to choose anything here); the only parameters chosen for this package (storage polarity pi, start planes 10, 61, 34, prefix seed label s3r6-ls128-v1) were set by cost objectives or fixed before any of our trials, never from a digest or masked-collision statistic; and our own runs of the experiment script were specified and hashed before our first trial of this family and are all reported, with the later reviewer runs, in proof Section 10.3, none selected, repeated or dropped according to its outcome.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability (Section 7) uses H1, through Pr[F1], Pr[F2] and Pr[Y1 >= E + floor(N^2/2^148) + 2^91] <= 2^-100 (Chebyshev); part (b) concerns only how the experimental support for (a) was obtained. The garbage-candidate part of the abort (<= 2^-61, Markov on E[Y2] <= N*2^-128 with a uniform run TAG), F3 (< 2^-545, counting), evaluator exactness, verification of every output, and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds are unconditional (the candidate cap makes the time bound hold in every run; the operation count is reproducible from proof Appendix A). For every z, P -> m(P, z) permutes the structured-prefix set (XORing z into the free lanes 4 and 14 keeps C4, C1 and the dependent lanes), so m(g, z) is uniform over that set for every z; cross-group pairs (all but a 2^-96 fraction of pairs) therefore provably collide with probability >= 2^-256 each (Cauchy-Schwarz), and the expected number of colliding pairs is at least (1-2^-96) N(N-1)/2^257 without H1; H1 is needed for the second-moment behaviour behind Pr[F1], for F2 and for Y1. Bitslicing, batching, the incremental round 2, the start planes, the dependency cone, the compiler, the 140-bit key, the fixed encodings, the 16-row transpose layout and the pair ids change neither the message set nor any digest value; they fix only the processing order, which depends on (batch, t, q) and never on digests.
heuristics.extrapolation: Tested at scale only: four organizer-executed scaled analogues with N_t = 2^9 messages and an 18-bit mask of kept digest bits (N_t^2/2^18 = 1, close to N^2/2^256 = (255/256)^2), all on structured 128-byte prefixes and computing digests with an evaluator that shares the counted program's geometry (linear-structure incremental round 2 with the program's read-only flips, storage polarity and fixed patch expressions; lane-complement rounds with theta at the store and the start planes 10, 61, 34; rounds 4-5 computed in full, then every word outside the Lemma 10 cone replaced by an unrelated constant; last round on the 35 kept planes at the program's key rows; the rotating-frame zero-row transpose in the program's 16-row layout, checked against the full transpose; processing order; every key also run through the tagged-id table with pair ids and adversarial garbage): 256 groups x 2, 16 groups x 32, a single group of 512 and 4 groups x 128 with the varying z bits at 25..31 (bs4's layouts and masks, unchanged). Every organizer trial checks the whole 140-bit key against an independent direct sponge (its first 4 and one at every step t = 2^i), the exact 22-word all-ones support of each z-bit used, and the maintained A2 and round-3 input against a rebuild from the prefixes. Selection control (H1(b)): layouts, masks, N_t, trial counts and seed derivation are those of our public 949c283b and 5e73af65; the organizer's public-seed run of this package should give manifest_sha256 6955f6ae, full_report_sha256 d160f2ea and 91 / 99 / 105 / 105 of 256 (full-width / spread / single-group / high-z), as our replay R1 did (the same replay reproduced the organizer's bs6 report hash 83e80e0e exactly; full hashes in proof Section 10.3). Participant-reported runs (untrusted): script and manifest frozen and the run plan hashed before our first trial of this family (proof Appendix B); three holdout nonces drawn afterwards gave 113 / 102 / 100 / 101, 105 / 107 / 101 / 92 and 96 / 107 / 104 / 104; the script's local mode with 12,288 trials per layout gave 4,845 / 4,861 / 4,804 / 4,849; after the build our review committee replayed the public seed twice (byte-identical to R1, not new samples) and ran one more holdout nonce (bc71146c, not pre-registered): 93 / 86 / 96 / 105. Pooled over all 13,568 trials per layout: z = +0.17 / +0.51 / -0.41 / +0.40 against the uniform-model value 0.393074; exact two-sided Clopper-Pearson intervals at the Bonferroni level 1 - 0.05/28 (28 comparisons: 4 layouts x 6 runs + 4 pooled) contain the model value in all 28, smallest exact p-value (twice the smaller tail) 0.069; the pre-registered analysis of the first five runs (24 comparisons) gave all 24 and smallest p 0.130. Masked-pair mean 1.0010 times the uniform value over all 54,272 trials (1.0022 +- 0.0061, variance/mean 0.994, over the 53,248 pre-registered ones), consistent with Var[Y1] <= E[Y1]. Every run of the script is listed. The claim extrapolates uniform-model behaviour to N = 255*2^120, the 256-bit digest and its 140-bit truncation.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is not proved. Within a group, round 1 is linear in z and A2 = A2(0) XOR sum_j z_j E_j with fixed group-independent vectors E_j (all-ones on 22 words; Lemmas 1-3), a stronger structure than in a generic search; five further nonlinear chi layers (rounds 2-6) follow, but masked low-width experiments cannot exclude a structural effect that appears only at full width. Within a group the digest has degree at most 2^5 = 32 in z; z has 32 bits, so no degree-based zero-sum exists on any affine subspace of z. The experiments use a full dictionary of masked keys, so the table loss F2 and the candidate count Y1 are bounded only under H1. Part (b) rests partly on checkable facts (the unchanged organizer configuration, the externally fixed family, cost-only parameter choices reproducible from proof Appendix A, the R1 report hash the organizer's public-seed run should reproduce) and partly on our statement about our own runs, whose timing cannot be checked; organizer seeds are public, and a holdout-nonce rerun by the organizer (supported without any change to the script) is the independent check. The intervals assume independent trials (distinct per-trial seeds, disjoint bit positions). The 0.00106 allowance between the model value 0.39106 and the claimed 0.39 is not statistically certified: the pooled experiments resolve the success frequency only to about +-0.008 per layout. F4 is the most sensitive use of H1: by Cauchy-Schwarz any non-uniformity of the 140-bit key can only raise E[Y1], and the cap VCAP tolerates a relative excess of 2^-7 (0.78%) over N^2/2^141, while the experiments resolve the masked-pair mean only to about 0.6%; within-group pairs would need an average key-collision probability above about 2^-51, or above about 2^-19 for the pairs of one z-difference, to matter.
